newsitem.title: UK: UK firms await new rules on corporate behaviour.
newsitem.headline: UK firms await new rules on corporate behaviour.

text.p: British companies and shareholders will on Tuesday hear the result of an 18-month inquiry into corporate governance which is widely tipped to soften previous regulation.

The preliminary report by the Hampel committee is due to be released at 1300 GMT on Tuesday, and British newspapers suggest it will urge a shift from detailed regulation towards a set of broad principles.
The committee was set up in November 1995 under ICI chairman Sir Ronald Hampel, and follows the work of two previous committees into the thorny area of how companies and shareholders should behave.
A report by Sir Adrian Cadbury covered corporate structures, while a later inquiry by Sir Richard Greenbury delved into boardroom pay.

While members of the Hampel committee will not comment on the report before its release, newspapers have said it will stress corporate governance is not just about accountability but also about business prosperity.
Within its 40 pages it will, however, emphasise disclosure and the importance of teamwork at the top.
Newspapers said the report will say institutional investors should draw up a policy on how to use their votes at company annual meetings.
And if they are right in their forecasts, Hampel will also recommend smaller companies should not enjoy a lighter corporate governance code, with the principles the same for all firms.

The Financial Times said the report will also say directors should continue to check they have a proper system of internal controls to stop fraud. And the system of one board of company directors should stay rather than become a two-tier system, the paper said.
A spokesman for the committee declined to comment on the newspaper reports, while investment advisory body Pirc said it was not commenting until after the preliminary report is made public.
